Cc: AWS Marketplace Ops <marketplace-ops@aws.amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace listing launch: procurement checklist & private offer specifics

Hi Rishi,

We're getting close to the go-live for the AWS Marketplace listing and have a few procurement and technical questions we need resolved before we can sign the PO: 

- Private Offer flow: can you confirm whether Acme will receive a single consolidated invoice from AWS or separate invoices from Redwood? We need billing alignment for our finance team.
- Trial configuration: is the 14-day trial enforced via Private Offer only, or can we do a time-limited entitlement on the public SKU?
- Metering model: we'd prefer a usage-based SKU (token/hour) but need guidance on minimum commit language and refunds for unused committed capacity.
- Procurement docs: please send SOC 2 summary, current SLA, and a one-page technical AMI/deployment note for our infra team.

We'd like to keep the timeline for signature this week if possible (PO targeted by Fri 11/26). Please advise and attach the requested docs.

Thanks,

Alicia Gomez
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corp

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, AWS Marketplace Ops <marketplace-ops@aws.amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing launch: procurement checklist & private offer specifics

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and attaching the docs you requested. See inline for next steps.

1) Billing / Invoicing: For Private Offers, AWS issues the consolidated invoice to Acme and remits Redwood's share through the AWS billing flow. If you require a vendor invoice from Redwood directly, we can provide a vendor invoice on request and support reconciliation reports monthly. (attachment: redwood-sla-v1.2.pdf)

2) Trial configuration: The 14-day trial can be enforced either as a Private Offer entitlement (recommended for enterprise trials) or via time-limited SKU on the public listing. For enterprise procurement and to avoid accidental public signups, we recommend Private Offer entitlements.

3) Metering & minimums: We support usage-based SKUs (per-token + request) and can layer a monthly commit. Commits are handled via the Private Offer terms; we can include a pro-rata refund or credit clause for unused committed capacity — sample language in the attached SLA.

4) Procurement docs: attaching SOC 2 summary and a short AMI deployment note for your infra team.

Attachments: redwood-sla-v1.2.pdf, soc2-summary-2026.pdf, ami-deploy-quickstart.txt

Next steps:
- Kimberly, Marissa: can you confirm the minimum-commit language we prefer and whether we want to offer the pro-rata credit (yes/no)?
- Aditya: please prepare a draft vendor invoice template in case Acme wants Redwood-issued invoices.
- Alicia: once you confirm billing preference, we'll upload the Private Offer to AWS and share the DocuSign PO link. Targeting signature by Fri 11/26 as requested.

+1 on recommending Private Offer entitlement for the trial — keeps the public funnel clean and prevents accidental consumption.

On minimum commit & refunds: propose we offer a 3-month rolling credit (credit only, no cash refunds) for unused committed spend for standard enterprise deals; for strategic pilots we can do pro-rata refunds case-by-case. I've pulled sample wording and added to the SLA (see redwood-sla-v1.2.pdf).

I'll also validate SKU metering descriptors with the product team and send a short FAQ for the field to reference.
